extracted.intended_audience: NIAID staff (program officers, grants management specialists) and NIH grantees (principal investigators and institutional sponsored research offices)
extracted.subtask_short: RPPR submission and review for NIAID grants
extracted.subtask_description: Standard operating procedure for preparing, submitting, reviewing, and approving Research Performance Progress Reports (RPPRs) for NIAID noncompeting grants, describing roles and responsibilities for grantee institutions, PIs, program officers, and grants management specialists. Covers required report content, compliance checks, documentation, and timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual progress report content
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH grantees must submit annual reports describing scientific progress and identifying changes in objectives, scope, or key personnel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include scientific progress for the past budget period and explicitly identify any changes in objectives, project scope, or key personnel. Follow institutional processes for completing the RPPR; PIs can be delegated this responsibility by their institution. Report supplements separately only if the Notice of Award specifies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiyear awards reporting rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiyear awards receive all funding in the first year and have different rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you have a multiyear funded (MYF) award, follow the NIH Instructions for Progress Reports for Multiyear Funded (MYF) Awards rather than standard annual RPPR procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness and completeness of RPPR
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH does not notify grantees that a progress report is late, and will delay awards until all reporting elements are complete.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the RPPR and all required elements are submitted and complete by the due date. Missing or incomplete reporting elements will delay award processing; correct any errors promptly to avoid award delays.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institution responsibilities for RPPR submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Confirm that the RPPR is enabled in your institutional eRA Commons profile and establish an internal process to fill out and submit RPPRs. Responsibility may be delegated to PIs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If RPPR is not enabled in your institutional eRA Commons profile, contact the eRA Service Desk. Institutions should set up a reliable workflow (sponsored research office or equivalent) to prepare and submit RPPRs and to track due dates.

rubrics_metrics.name: PI responsibilities for RPPR
rubrics_metrics.description: Principal Investigators must use eRA Commons to get a list of progress reports and their due dates and follow the process established by their sponsored research office to fill out and submit the RPPR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PIs should check eRA Commons for report listings and deadlines, adhere to institutional submission procedures, and only submit report supplements separately if the Notice of Award instructs them to do so.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rigor and reproducibility reporting requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Address Rigor and Reproducibility in research and career development progress reports, as well as in fellowship and training progress reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain the approaches taken to ensure robust and unbiased results and describe efforts you plan to take to ensure scientific rigor and robustness going forward. Include this content in applicable progress report sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public access compliance in RPPR
rubrics_metrics.description: Check public access compliance using the Progress Report Additional Materials (PRAM) link in eRA Commons and correct any errors in your records.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use PRAM to verify compliance with NIH public access policy. If NIH notifies you about noncompliant publications, respond promptly through eRA Commons; NIH cannot issue your award until every error is corrected. See the Public Access of Publications SOP and My Bibliography resources for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclude IRB/IACUC approval dates from RPPR
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not provide institutional review board (IRB) and institutional animal care and use committee (IACUC) approval dates in the RPPR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If NIH needs IRB or IACUC approval dates, your institution will provide that information upon request. See the Human Subjects Certifications: IRB or IEC SOP and Animals in Research Grants SOP for more information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program officer evaluation of scientific progress
rubrics_metrics.description: Program officers must review progress reports to evaluate scientific progress during the past budget period and request additional information from the PI if necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the project is meeting objectives and whether additional clarification or details are needed. Use findings to inform decisions about continued funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program officer determination of scope changes (human subjects)
rubrics_metrics.description: Program officers must determine whether there has been a change in scope due to documented changes in the use of human subjects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify any documented shifts in human subjects involvement that alter project scope and document those determinations; request further information from the PI when necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program officer verification of public access and justification for funding
rubrics_metrics.description: Program officers must verify PIs have complied with public access rules and confirm that NIAID still has justification for funding the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check PRAM/eRA records for public access compliance and assess whether the scientific progress justifies continued support. Document deficiencies and follow up as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program officer documentation using Program Officer Checklist
rubrics_metrics.description: Document your review and approval or disapproval of progress reports using the Program Officer Checklist in eRA’s Program Management Module.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Generate Checklists by the 10th of the month before the grant anniversary date. Use the Program Signoff Notes section to document approval/disapproval of changes in staffing, personnel effort, changes in scope, or plans to use funds in the upcoming budget period, and to identify issues requiring follow-up by grants management specialists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grants management specialist administrative and fiscal evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: Grants Management Specialists must evaluate the grant's administrative and fiscal status and perform an administrative and fiscal evaluation using information in the progress report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Access the Program Officer Checklist from the IMPAC Grants Management module, review the program officer's recommendations and checklist items that require follow-up, and resolve all checklist items before issuing an award. See the GMP Non-Competing Progress Reports (eSNAPs and SNAPs) SOP for more responsibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approval requirement before award issuance
rubrics_metrics.description: Both the NIAID program officer and the grants management specialist must approve a progress report before NIAID can issue an award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not issue awards until all Program Officer Checklist items and any grants management follow-up items are resolved; unresolved checklist items will prevent award issuance.
